transcript.answer:
Otto maps TMS error kinds to escalation triggers in `ESCALATION_BY_KIND`, in `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts`. It is a `Record<TmsErrorKind, EscalationTrigger | null>` covering the nine `TmsError` kinds from `@support-agent/tms-client`. A kind with no row fails `npm run typecheck`. Results carry only the kind, never the TMS message text.

Two kinds escalate:
- `unavailable` (a 5xx) marks `tms_unavailable`.
- `timeout` marks `tms_timeout`.

The other TMS kinds map to `null`, so they render an error or not-found card without escalating. These are `not_found`, `rate_limited`, `network`, `invalid_response`, `unauthorized` and `forbidden`. The error table I could read was cut off partway through the `forbidden` row, so I did not see the ninth kind. I am assuming it is also `null`.

There is a third escalation in `get_booking_status`, but it is not part of the kind mapping. It is `customer_scope_conflict`, raised by the tool's own ownership check when an order's shipment names a payer or orderer that differs from the order's. It is not one of the nine TMS error kinds.

judgements.reason: The answer says only two kinds escalate and that customer_scope_conflict is not part of the kind mapping, but the gold has ESCALATION_BY_KIND keyed by TmsFailureKind and includes customer_scope_conflict as a third escalating kind.
